hazards.reason: Copying order holds the database's write lock for time that grows with the table.
hazards.subject: table/order

hazards.reason: Order.details changes from a JSON value (TEXT) to a scalar (TEXT): servers built from the previous version still read and write a JSON value (TEXT).
hazards.subject: table/order/column/details

hazards.reason: SQLite's ALTER TABLE cannot change the type of details, so the step rebuilds order: it copies the rows into a new table, drops the old one and renames the new one, with foreign keys off.
hazards.subject: table/order

statements:
CREATE TABLE "_new_order" (
  "id" TEXT DEFAULT (lower(hex(randomblob(4)) || '-' || hex(randomblob(2)) || '-4' || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || substr('89ab', 1 + (random() & 3), 1) || substr(hex(randomblob(2)), 2) || '-' || hex(randomblob(6)))) NOT NULL,
  "code" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "customer_id" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "total" INTEGER NOT NULL,
  "reference" TEXT,
  "note" TEXT,
  "placed_at" TEXT DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')) NOT NULL,
  "details" TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY ("id"),
  FOREIGN KEY ("customer_id") REFERENCES "customer" ("id") ON DELETE RESTRICT
)
steps.subject: table/order
